<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Description>
      The official .NET library for extended OpenAI API capabilities in Microsoft Foundry, including those used by the Foundry Agents Service.

      This library features derived clients, new compatible types, and a variety of extension elements that facilitate easier use of new Microsoft
      Foundry API surfaces. It depends on and builds from the official OpenAI library for .NET to maintain rapid upstream feature propagation and
      ongoing forward compatibility.
    </Description>
    <AssemblyTitle>Microsoft Foundry OpenAI .NET Extensions</AssemblyTitle>
    <Version>3.0.0-beta.6</Version>
    <PackageTags>Azure.AI.Extensions.OpenAI</PackageTags>
    <TargetFrameworks>$(RequiredTargetFrameworks)</TargetFrameworks>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <IncludeOperationsSharedSource>true</IncludeOperationsSharedSource>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <IncludeSystemClientModelSharedSourceForTracing>true</IncludeSystemClientModelSharedSourceForTracing>
  </PropertyGroup>
  
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="OpenAI" />
    <PackageReference Include="Azure.Core" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)ExperimentalAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

proposals.subtype: Construct A2A call items through kind-only base constructors
proposals.explanation: The constructor family initializes call fields and chains to ResponseItemKind.A2APreviewCall, or the supplied kind in the type-taking internal overload. Only that latter overload calls ApplyAgentAttribution; the other internal overload accepts id/agentReference/responseId without using them in its body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This Custom partial supplies the constructor bodies and explicitly identifies the type-taking constructor as relocated and changed to a kind-only base call.

proposals.subtype: Construct A2A output items through kind-only base constructors
proposals.explanation: The public and internal constructor family chains to A2APreviewCallOutput or an explicitly supplied kind and assigns call/name/status/output fields as applicable. The type-taking overload calls ApplyAgentAttribution and retains additional properties; the earlier internal overload does not use its id/agentReference/responseId arguments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete constructors live in Custom and the type-taking overload has an explicit relocation/base-constructor customization comment.

proposals.subtype: Replace the generated single-name constructor with an optional-version constructor
proposals.explanation: CodeGenSuppress targets AgentReference(string); the handwritten constructor takes name and optional version, assigns Name/Version and creates a ChangeTrackingDictionary for additional properties. It performs no explicit name validation in the supplied body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A suppression attribute and concrete replacement constructor are supplied in the Custom partial.

proposals.subtype: Expose the mapped agent version as a get-only string
proposals.explanation: The partial explicitly supplies a public get-only string Version property mapped by CodeGenMember("Version"). Its value can be assigned by the supplied constructor; the generated property's original type or mutability is not shown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom source defines the property and its CodeGenMember mapping rather than merely documenting it.

proposals.subtype: Convert a string identifier implicitly to an agent reference
proposals.explanation: The implicit conversion operator constructs AgentReference from the supplied agentName, using the optional version constructor's default. It does not parse an encoded version or explicitly reject null.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A concrete conversion operator is implemented in the Custom partial.

proposals.subtype: Map the structured-output model to the agent response-item name
proposals.explanation: CodeGenType("StructuredOutputsOutputItem") maps that generated model name onto the AgentStructuredOutputsResponseItem partial type.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial contains an explicit CodeGenType mapping with a different source model name.

proposals.subtype: Construct structured-output response items with a fixed or supplied kind
proposals.explanation: The public BinaryData constructor delegates with null attribution/additional-property arguments. Internal constructors assign Output and additional properties while chaining to StructuredOutputs or a supplied kind; only the type-taking overload calls ApplyAgentAttribution.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete constructor adapters are implemented in the Custom partial outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Map the workflow-action output model onto the preview response-item type
proposals.explanation: CodeGenType("WorkflowActionOutputItem") binds that generated model name to AgentWorkflowPreviewActionResponseItem.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An explicit different-name CodeGenType attribute appears in the Custom partial.

proposals.subtype: Expose mapped workflow status as a nullable get-only typed value
proposals.explanation: CodeGenMember("Status") maps a public get-only AgentWorkflowPreviewActionStatus? property. The supplied constructors populate it, but the baseline generated status representation is not captured.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial explicitly declares the mapped property and its nullable typed API.

proposals.subtype: Construct workflow-action items through fixed or supplied response kinds
proposals.explanation: Constructors chain to WorkflowAction or the supplied kind and assign action-kind, identifiers, links and status according to their parameters. The type-taking internal overload additionally calls ApplyAgentAttribution; its id parameter is not read in the body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete Custom constructor bodies include an explicit comment identifying the type-taking constructor's relocation and base-call change.

proposals.subtype: Normalize recognized response-item discriminators through the Azure serialization context
proposals.explanation: AsAgentResponseItem round-trips an item through ModelReaderWriter with WireOptions and AzureAIExtensionsOpenAIContext. The predicate requests conversion only for non-null items whose kind resolves through TryGetAzureItemType and whose runtime type is not already that result. NormalizeAgentOutputItems replaces matching entries only in a non-null writable output list; the private single-item adapter reuses the same predicate.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom extension code implements the predicate, explicit serialization round-trip and in-place output-list traversal.

proposals.subtype: Normalize recognized echoed tool discriminators through the Azure serialization context
proposals.explanation: The tool round-trip writes/reads ResponseTool through the Azure context. Its predicate checks the known-kind lookup and current runtime type; NormalizeAgentTools replaces matching elements only in a non-null writable tools list. A private NormalizeAgentResponseTool adapter implements the same conditional conversion, but no caller of that adapter is shown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom extension methods implement concrete tool serialization, runtime-type checks and list mutation.

proposals.subtype: Dispatch streaming update variants into item or whole-response normalization
proposals.explanation: NormalizeStreamingUpdate replaces added/done Item values through the item adapter, and normalizes both item/tool lists on completed, created, in-progress, queued, incomplete and failed response snapshots. It returns the same update; unmatched update types pass through. The composed response helper calls the two list normalizers.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A concrete switch over streaming update types and composed response helper are implemented in Custom.

proposals.subtype: Create responses for an existing conversation with a selected agent and no input member
proposals.explanation: The sync/async extension pair constructs options from agentRef and conversation.Id, serializes them, removes the JSON input member, and calls the BinaryContent protocol overload using cancellation-derived or new RequestOptions. Both cast the result to ResponseResult, normalize it and preserve the raw response in ClientResult.FromValue. The async path uses ConfigureAwait(false).
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom public extension overloads and the RemoveItems helper implement explicit option construction, JSON editing and result projection.

proposals.subtype: Read the Azure-specific file status from serialized wire JSON
proposals.explanation: GetAzureFileStatus serializes an OpenAIFile with WireOptions, parses its JSON and returns _sdk_status when GetString yields a nonempty string; otherwise it returns null. It does not catch serialization, parse or wrong-JSON-kind errors, so this is not a general safe-status parser.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom public extension implements an explicit wire round-trip and extra-property lookup.

proposals.subtype: Construct search call items through fixed or supplied kinds
proposals.explanation: The constructor family chains to AzureAISearchCall or a supplied kind and initializes call/arguments/status fields. The type-taking internal overload calls ApplyAgentAttribution and retains additional properties; the earlier internal overload does not consume id/agentReference/responseId in its body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom constructor implementations include an explicit relocation and kind-only base-call customization comment.

proposals.subtype: Construct search output items through fixed or supplied kinds
proposals.explanation: The constructor family initializes call/status/output fields as applicable, with AzureAISearchCallOutput or an explicitly supplied kind passed to base. Only the type-taking overload invokes ApplyAgentAttribution; the earlier internal overload's attribution/id parameters are unused in its body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial contains concrete constructors and an explicit base-call relocation customization comment.

proposals.subtype: Chain the deserialization constructor to the function-tool kind
proposals.explanation: The internal parameterless AzureFunctionTool constructor explicitly calls ResponseToolKind.AzureFunction on the base class. Its empty body is not the behavior being counted; the discriminator-bearing base initializer is.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial explicitly supplies the base initializer and comments that it replaces missing generated constructor chaining.

proposals.subtype: Construct function call items through fixed or supplied kinds
proposals.explanation: Constructors assign call/name/arguments/status fields and chain to AzureFunctionCall or the supplied kind. The type-taking internal overload calls ApplyAgentAttribution and retains additional properties; the earlier internal overload does not use id/agentReference/responseId in its body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete Custom constructors include an explicit relocation and kind-only base-call customization comment.

decisions.reason: The Custom partial declares the constructor family at lines 19-70, including fixed and supplied ResponseItemKind base calls; the supplied-kind overload applies attribution while the earlier internal overload does not use its id, agentReference or responseId parameters. Constructor adaptation is a reusable generator-addressable model shape. The comment's account of the generated constructor is not independently verified.

Lines 18-68 declare actual Custom output-item constructors, including a supplied-kind base call with attribution and an earlier internal overload that leaves attribution inputs unused. The model constructor pattern and cited range fit; the stated generated-code history is supported only by a source comment.

CodeGenSuppress at line 10 names the string constructor, and the Custom replacement at lines 20-25 adds optional version, initializes the properties and creates the additional-property dictionary. This is a plausible generator-addressable constructor customization; no generated baseline or explicit name validation is needed for the stated observation.

The Custom partial declares a mapped public get-only string Version at lines 13-15, which the supplied constructor assigns. The pattern describes the read-only property shape rather than a service name; the uncaptured generated property's prior shape is correctly left uncertain.

The Custom partial declares an implicit string-to-AgentReference conversion at lines 27-30, constructing the model directly from the name; no parsing or null check appears there. It is a distinct handwritten model API from the constructor itself and plausibly generator-addressable.

The CodeGenType attribute at lines 12-13 explicitly maps StructuredOutputsOutputItem to a differently named Custom partial class. A generated-model name mapping is a reusable generator-addressable API-shape override; no claims about the uncaptured generated implementation are required.

Lines 17-49 implement public and internal Custom constructors with fixed or supplied kind base calls, output/additional-property assignment and attribution on only the supplied-kind overload. This is distinct from the model's CodeGenType name mapping; the constructor shape could plausibly be generated.

Lines 12-13 contain the CodeGenType mapping from WorkflowActionOutputItem to the differently named Custom partial. The cited declaration supports a reusable generator-addressable model-name override, separate from the status property and constructors.

The Custom partial explicitly declares a CodeGenMember-mapped, nullable, get-only typed Status at lines 15-17, assigned in the supplied constructors. The proposal does not assert an unobserved generated baseline; read-only mapped model properties are a plausible generator-addressable pattern.

The Custom constructor declarations and bodies at lines 23-77 show fixed/supplied response kinds, action identifiers, nullable status and attribution only in the supplied-kind overload; its id parameter is unused. The explanation describes this distinct constructor adaptation without treating the comment's generated-code history as established.

Lines 30-50 implement the item wire round-trip and discriminator/type gate; lines 82-104 mutate only a writable response output list when that gate succeeds. This is handwritten polymorphic serialization normalization in Custom, a reusable generator-addressable shape. Actual completeness of the uncaptured discriminator dispatch table is not claimed.

Lines 54-72 implement a tool wire round-trip, known-kind gate and conditional adapter, while lines 113-135 mutate only eligible writable tool lists. This is distinct from output-item normalization; the proposal correctly notes that no caller of the private adapter is shown in this evidence.

NormalizeStreamingUpdate at lines 158-190 explicitly handles added/done item updates and six response lifecycle snapshots and returns the update; lines 141-146 compose the existing item/tool normalizers. The streaming dispatch is a separate handwritten behavior from the non-streaming normalization primitives.

Lines 199-246 implement public sync/async conversation-based response overloads and the shared JSON input-removal helper, then call the protocol methods and project normalized typed results with the raw response. The pair represents one convenience behavior; a generator could plausibly emit the options-to-protocol bridge.

The public Custom extension at lines 251-266 serializes the file with wire options, reads the _sdk_status property and returns its nonempty string or null. This is a distinct handwritten wire-property accessor; the proposal appropriately does not claim it handles invalid JSON kinds or serialization errors.

The Custom search-call constructors at lines 18-64 implement fixed/supplied kinds and field assignments, with attribution only in the supplied-kind overload. The earlier internal overload leaves its id and attribution arguments unused; the common constructor shape is plausibly generator-addressable, while the relocation account is only a source comment.

Lines 17-62 show Custom search-output constructors with fixed/supplied kinds, output/status assignment as applicable and attribution only in the supplied-kind overload. They support a separate output-model constructor customization, without independently proving the comment's claimed generator failure.

The Custom partial's internal deserialization constructor at lines 17-20 explicitly calls base(ResponseToolKind.AzureFunction); the discriminator-bearing initializer, not the empty body, is the concrete customization. Constructor-chain generation is plausible, although the comment's prior generated behavior has not been independently checked.

Lines 19-70 declare and implement Custom function-call constructors, fixed or supplied kind initializers and assignments; only the supplied-kind overload applies attribution. The internal fixed-kind overload leaves id/agentReference/responseId unused. This is a distinct reusable constructor adaptation, not proof of the generated baseline described in a comment.

limitations: Only ten of 319 eligible source files are captured. Extensive Custom and telemetry source, generated models, serialization context, dispatch tables, client integration and imported OpenAI implementations are absent. No package-wide absence claim follows.

All captured files are Custom partials/extensions marked handwritten-marker. This establishes concrete handwritten contributions, but no generated counterpart or executed build proves the comments' stated compiler errors, the full original signatures or the exact upstream defect.

Several fixed-kind internal constructors accept id/agentReference/responseId without using them; the supplied-kind overloads call ApplyAgentAttribution only with agentReference, responseId and additional properties. That helper is excluded, so actual attribution storage or preservation is not established. No captured constructor reads id.

The response-item and tool normalization algorithms depend on excluded TryGetAzureItemType/TryGetAzureToolType tables and AzureAIExtensionsOpenAIContext. Their actual discriminator coverage, deserialized types, forward-compatibility and serialization round-trip fidelity are not verified. Read-only lists are deliberately skipped, not rewritten.

The captured conversation facade explicitly invokes response normalization. No caller of NormalizeStreamingUpdate, NormalizeAgentResponseTool or the broader streaming wrappers is supplied, so local helper behavior is not evidence that every client/stream path runs it.

NormalizeStreamingUpdate is an update-object adapter, not a captured SSE decoder, network stream implementation or backpressure mechanism. Its known snapshot cases do not establish support for all possible update types.

The public conversation facade dereferences conversation.Id and depends on excluded option serialization and ToRequestOptions behavior. Input removal is observable, but the server requirement, runtime cancellation semantics and actual HTTP exchange are not.

GetAzureFileStatus has no null input guard or exception catch and does not dispose its JsonDocument in the supplied body. The finding measures extra-property extraction rather than claiming a resilient or resource-complete parser.

ModuleMajor remains the frozen inventory identity 1 while metadata/source report 3.0.0-beta.5/3.0.0-beta.6. Stable metadata does not establish this pinned source as a stable release; identity/version reconciliation is deferred.

A2A, search and function calls here are model construction and attribution adapters, not executed tools, authentication policies or LRO pollers. No SDK code was executed and no causal motivation is asserted beyond explicitly attributed source comments.

Partial extraction: 10 captured source files out of 319 eligible files (451 discovered), with 93 explicitly skipped files. This review makes no claim about customizations outside the supplied evidence.

Generated counterparts, the OpenAI base classes, the attribution helper, discriminator dispatch implementations, call sites outside these snippets and runtime behavior are not supplied. Comments about generator errors or relocation and the cited context establish neither an independently verified root cause nor a verified fix.
Every accepted finding is AI-reviewed rather than human-verified; human overrides remain authoritative. The omission check was limited to the 10 supplied evidence items.
